label: Research laboratories and biosafety
description: The people who run and oversee research laboratories: biosafety officers, responsible officials of select agent registrations, laboratory directors, environmental health and safety, institutional biosafety committees, occupational health, research compliance and research IT. It covers a university biosafety program, a registered entity, a hospital or clinical research laboratory, an animal facility and a company or core facility. Exercises concern incident management, notification, continuity and compliance, never how to handle or make anything.

vocabulary.facility: the research laboratory (the lab suite, its freezers and cold rooms, the animal facility and the offices that oversee them)
vocabulary.public: the research community, participants in studies, neighbors of the campus, sponsors and the press
vocabulary.frontline: principal investigators, lab managers, technicians, graduate students, animal care staff and biosafety officers
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the incident command post, the biosafety office or the institution's emergency operations center

it: inventory management system with an audit trail (LIMS or spreadsheet)
freezer and incubator monitoring with alarm call-out
electronic lab notebook and sample tracking
instrument computers on a research network
mass notification and the emergency phone tree
shared services: email, directory and SIEM
ot: -80 degC freezers and liquid nitrogen supply

roles.name: Institutional Official / Vice President for Research
roles.description: Reports to NIH and sponsors, decides the institution's public posture, and holds the line between the laboratories and the university.

roles.name: Institutional Biosafety Committee chair
roles.description: Reviews incidents, orders corrective action and decides what the committee reports to NIH.

roles.name: Responsible Official
roles.description: Decides notification to the Federal Select Agent Program, completes the written report, restricts access and suspends work in registered areas.

roles.name: Alternate Responsible Official
roles.description: Acts for the RO when absent and shares the notification and report decisions.

roles.name: Biosafety Officer
roles.description: Classifies the incident, checks containment, refers workers for medical evaluation and reports to the committee.

roles.name: Environmental Health and Safety director
roles.description: Coordinates decontamination, waste, fire safety and the response of emergency services.

roles.name: Principal Investigator / Laboratory Director
roles.description: Orders stop-work in the lab, accounts for materials, reports exposures and owns corrective actions.

roles.name: Laboratory Manager
roles.description: Keeps inventory, access lists, freezer and equipment alarms and supplies; first to see most incidents.

roles.name: Core Facility or Clinical Laboratory Manager
roles.description: Runs a shared or clinical laboratory, decides what is moved or turned away during an incident and speaks for its users.

roles.name: Occupational Health physician or nurse
roles.description: Evaluates exposed workers, advises on post-exposure care and sets work restrictions.

roles.name: Research Compliance / IRB director
roles.description: Notifies the IRB, sponsors and regulators and decides how data and human subject incidents are reported.

roles.name: Research IT / Data Steward
roles.team: Team E: Research IT and Facilities
roles.description: Contains data incidents, restores from backups and secures instrument networks.

roles.name: Facilities and Security
roles.team: Team E: Research IT and Facilities
roles.description: Provides access logs, alarms, power and ventilation, and first response on the building.

roles.name: Animal Facility Director / Veterinarian
roles.description: Isolates colonies, decides on euthanasia and reports to the animal care committee.

roles.name: University Communications / Legal Counsel
roles.description: Drafts the public statement, handles media and reviews every outside notice.

outsideParties: CDC Division of Regulatory Science and Compliance and APHIS Agricultural Select Agent Services (the Federal Select Agent Program)
the local fire department and hazmat team
campus police and local law enforcement
the IRB and participants in affected studies
the vendor of the monitoring or inventory system
mediaChannels: a social post from a lab member

sceneAnchors.public: a university sidewalk outside a research building: students with backpacks, a hazard sign at a door, a news van at the curb, afternoon light
sceneAnchors.control: a biosafety office command post: a conference table with laptops, a printed floor plan with colored pins, a freezer alarm panel on a screen and a whiteboard with a phone tree
sceneAnchors.exterior: a loading dock at the back of a research building with a fire truck, a facilities worker with a clipboard and wet pavement under overcast sky

addedThreatFamilies.label: Laboratory exposure
addedThreatFamilies.description: A worker may have been exposed to an infectious agent through a needlestick, a spill outside containment or an equipment failure; the response runs from stop-work and medical evaluation to the reports each office owes.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: A worker reports a possible exposure and the first facts conflict about what happened and when.
beats: The worker tells the lab manager about a needlestick at the end of a shift
The PI says it was minor and asks to keep the lab running
A coworker saw a spill that the report does not mention

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Stop-work, first aid and the move to medical evaluation happen while the clock runs.
beats: The BSO asks who has stopped work in the room and who has been told to stay out
Occupational health is closed for the weekend and the on-call line goes to voicemail
A visitor was in the room and has not been identified

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: The BSO classifies the incident and works out who must be told and by when.
beats: The PI, occupational health and the IBC chair give conflicting advice on whether the event is reportable
The institution's own deadline for the PI to report is shorter than the funder's
An overt exposure to recombinant material raises an immediate notice to the funder

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team reconstructs what happened from the worker's account, the room records and the equipment log.
beats: The access log shows a second person in the lab
The equipment log shows the cabinet alarm was silenced earlier that week
Training records for the worker are out of date

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: The written reports are drafted and the facts must agree across them.
beats: The internal report, the IBC minutes and the funder notice give different times
Counsel asks to review the funder notice before it goes
A draft staff email says more than the report does

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The committee decides on corrective actions and who owns each one.
beats: The IBC asks for retraining and a room inspection
The PI disputes a work restriction
Facilities cannot service the cabinet for three weeks

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: The room and the worker return to work on stated conditions.
beats: Occupational health clears the worker with a follow-up schedule
The IBC lifts the stop-work order for part of the lab
A lessons-learned memo goes to every lab on the floor

decisionPointExamples: classify the event as reportable now, or wait for the occupational health evaluation
stop work in the whole suite, or only in the room
tell the funder today, or after the IBC meets
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an incident report timestamp, a badge-in record, an occupational health intake note, a training record, an equipment service log
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the on-call line is unanswered, the worker's account changes, the PI wants to keep working, records are on paper in the lab
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the BSO, occupational health, the IBC chair, the PI and the institutional official
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a classification, stop-work, medical evaluation or notification decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Inventory discrepancy
addedThreatFamilies.description: A count of registered material does not match the records; the response is to decide whether an item is missing, who is told and when, and how the records are reconciled inside the written report deadline.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: An audit finds that the count and the inventory record differ for one registered item.
beats: The lab manager's count is one short of the record
The last audit was clean eleven weeks ago
A new technician says the record was updated on paper

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Access is restricted and the room is secured while the team searches the obvious places.
beats: The RO asks who has the freezer key and the access list
Security pulls the door log for the past month
A search of the freezer finds an unlabeled box

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: The responsible official decides whether this is a possible theft or loss and which calls are due immediately.
beats: The RO has to choose between waiting for the search and calling now
The alternate RO is on leave and the phone tree is out of date
Law enforcement is on the immediate notification list

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team reconciles records against transfers, destruction logs and the freezer contents.
beats: A transfer was recorded in one system and not in the other
A destruction was logged by one person and signed by no one
The audit trail shows an edit after hours

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: The written report is prepared inside seven calendar days and the facts must agree.
beats: Form 3 information is incomplete on day five
The PI's account of the transfer differs from the log
Counsel asks to see the draft

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The entity corrects its record keeping and its plan.
beats: The RO proposes dual sign-off on every transfer
The inventory system cannot enforce it
The entity must review its incident response plan after the event

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: Work resumes under the stated conditions and the plan is revised.
beats: The RO lifts access restrictions in steps
A drill record is written for the plan review
The next audit is moved up

decisionPointExamples: notify now on a possible loss, or finish the search first
restrict the whole lab or one freezer
report the item as lost or as a records error
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an inventory record with a gap, a transfer slip, a destruction log, a door log, an audit trail entry
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: records are held in two systems, the person who handled the item has left, the RO is unreachable
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the responsible official, the alternate, the BSO, security and the PI
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a notification, restriction or reporting decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Freezer failure and sample loss
addedThreatFamilies.description: A freezer or incubator alarm fails or goes unanswered and irreplaceable samples are at risk; the team decides what to save first and whom to call.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: A temperature alarm sounds or a technician finds a warm freezer on a weekend.
beats: The monitoring system shows an alarm that nobody acknowledged
The call-out list reaches a number that has changed
A door was left ajar after a late delivery

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Staff move what they can to backup space while the alarm clock runs.
beats: The backup freezer is nearly full
The lab manager must choose between two racks
Facilities cannot reach the building until morning

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: The lab decides what is irreplaceable, who must be told and what the sponsor needs to hear.
beats: A collaborator's samples are in the same freezer
The institutional official wants a loss estimate before facts are known
Insurance requires notice inside a stated period

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team finds the cause and checks the monitoring and call-out systems.
beats: The monitoring log shows a sensor offline for a day
The compressor service record is overdue
The power log shows a short outage

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Reports go to the sponsor, the institution and the insurer, and the loss register is closed.
beats: The register lists samples as lost that were found in a backup
A sponsor asks whether the study can continue
Participant consent terms limit what can be re-collected

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The lab changes alarms, call-out and backup space.
beats: Facilities proposes a second sensor on every unit
Budget for a backup freezer is not approved
The call-out list is tested monthly from now on

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: The lab restocks and resumes work.
beats: Replacement samples are collected where possible
The register is reconciled with the freezer contents
A summary goes to every lab that shares the room

decisionPointExamples: move the most valuable rack first, or the largest group
wait for facilities, or move samples to an unqualified freezer
tell the sponsor tonight, or after the count
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an alarm log, a temperature trend, a call-out record, a sample register entry, a service record
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the alarm does not reach anyone, backup space is short, nobody holds the key to the cold room
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the lab manager, the PI, facilities, the sponsor liaison and research compliance
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a decision on what to move, whom to call or what to tell the sponsor

addedThreatFamilies.label: Laboratory facility emergency
addedThreatFamilies.description: A fire, flood, loss of ventilation or power affects a laboratory building with active work; the response is evacuation, coordination with responders and the plan for the work left behind.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: An alarm sounds and people are working with open experiments.
beats: The fire alarm sounds during an active run
The building automation system shows ventilation off
A flooded floor reaches the cold room

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Staff evacuate, secure what they can and meet responders with a facility briefing.
beats: A lab manager asks whether to leave an experiment running
The fire department asks what is stored on the floor
Two people are missing from the muster list

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: The incident commander and the BSO classify the event and notify the offices that must be told.
beats: The RO has to decide whether the event touches registered areas
The institutional official wants a statement
Neighbors are asking about smoke

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team checks the building's systems, access records and the state of each room.
beats: The ventilation log shows when airflow stopped
Door records show which rooms were open
Responders report water in an animal room

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Reports are filed with the institution, insurers and any registration.
beats: The facilities report and the lab report disagree on the time
A sponsor needs a statement on research impact
Counsel reviews the press statement

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The institution repairs, retests and revises the plan.
beats: The building cannot be reoccupied for a week
Backup power failed its last test
The plan's responder briefing sheet was out of date

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: Rooms are cleared for reoccupancy in order.
beats: The BSO signs off a room only after checks
Staff are briefed before return
The plan is revised after the event

decisionPointExamples: let responders in before the BSO arrives, or wait
evacuate the whole building, or the wing
issue a public statement now, or after the count
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an alarm panel event, a building automation log, a muster list, a door record, a responder report
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the BSO is off site, the muster list is out of date, responders do not know the building
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: incident command, the BSO, facilities, the fire department and communications
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: an evacuation, responder or notification decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Animal facility emergency
addedThreatFamilies.description: An animal facility loses environmental control, has an escape or a colony health event; the response mixes animal welfare, containment and the reports the program owes.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: Husbandry staff find a failure or an event in an animal room.
beats: A room's temperature alarm sounded overnight
A cage was found open in a corridor
The veterinarian reports an unexpected cluster of sick animals

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Staff secure rooms, protect animals and limit movement between rooms.
beats: The facility director must choose which rooms to isolate
An investigator wants to retrieve a study group
Staff are told to stay in their rooms

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: The director and the committee classify the event and decide whom to tell.
beats: The animal care committee has a reporting duty
A sponsor study is affected
An accrediting body expects notice of significant events

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team finds the cause from facility logs and records.
beats: The building system log shows a fan fault
A door log shows an unlocked room
A health record shows earlier signs

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Reports go to the committee, the sponsor and the institution.
beats: The report to the committee and the sponsor differ in numbers
Counsel reviews wording about animal welfare
A press inquiry reaches communications

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The facility fixes its controls and plans.
beats: The facility proposes a second alarm path
Funding for repairs is delayed
Husbandry staff ask for clearer call-out

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: Rooms reopen in order and studies resume.
beats: The veterinarian clears rooms one at a time
Investigators re-plan studies
The committee reviews the event

decisionPointExamples: isolate the whole barrier or one room
euthanize a study group, or wait for the veterinarian
tell the sponsor now, or with the committee report
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an environmental alarm log, a husbandry record, a veterinary note, a door log, a census sheet
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: alarm call-out fails, staff are short, investigators push to reach their animals
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the facility director, the veterinarian, the committee chair, the PI and facilities
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: an isolation, welfare or reporting decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Research data breach
addedThreatFamilies.description: Ransomware or unauthorized access reaches instrument computers or a study database; the team contains the incident and meets the notification duties to the IRB, sponsors, participants and regulators.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: An instrument computer shows a ransom note or an alert shows unusual access to a study database.
beats: A technician reports a locked instrument computer
The data steward sees large transfers from a lab share
A collaborator reports that a shared folder is encrypted

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Research IT isolates systems while labs decide what to do with runs in progress.
beats: Research IT asks to power off the instrument network
A time-critical run is under way
Backups for the notebook system are two days old

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: Compliance works out whose data is involved and which notices are due.
beats: Participant records are on one instrument computer
The sponsor contract names a notice period
Counsel asks whether protected health information is involved

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The team establishes what was accessed and what can be restored.
beats: The log shows access from an unknown address
Backup status shows a gap
A collaborator holds a copy of the data

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Notices go to the IRB, the sponsor and, where required, participants and regulators.
beats: The IRB notice and the participant letter state different counts
A state deadline is shorter than the sponsor's
Communications drafts a statement for staff

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: Research IT and compliance change controls.
beats: Instrument computers cannot take patches without vendor approval
Segmenting the instrument network delays a study
Training for data stewards is scheduled

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: Systems return in order and studies resume.
beats: Instruments come back one at a time
The IRB reviews the corrective plan
A summary goes to every principal investigator

decisionPointExamples: pay or restore from backup
tell participants now, or finish the scope first
power off the instrument network, or keep the run going
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an access log, a backup status, an instrument network diagram, a ransom note, a data inventory
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: instrument vendors control patching, backups are old, the data inventory is incomplete
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: research IT, the data steward, research compliance, the IRB, counsel and the sponsor liaison
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a restore, isolation or notification decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Workplace violence or threat
addedThreatFamilies.description: A threat, suspicious package or aggressive visitor puts a laboratory building and its restricted areas at risk; the response protects people and controls access.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: A threat or a suspicious item is reported near a laboratory.
beats: A threatening voicemail names a researcher
A package arrives with no sender
A visitor argues with a technician at the door

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Security protects people and restricts access to sensitive areas.
beats: Security asks which rooms need to be locked
The RO asks to confirm registered areas are secured
A researcher is working alone

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: Leaders classify the threat and decide whom to tell.
beats: Police ask for a building plan
The institutional official wants a statement
The RO asks whether the event counts as a security breach

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: Security and campus police gather facts and review recordings.
beats: Camera footage is from the wrong door
A badge was used at an odd hour
An earlier email carries a similar message

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Reports go to police, the institution and any registration.
beats: The security report and police report differ
A researcher asks for protection
Communications drafts a notice to staff

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The institution revises access and training.
beats: Visitor policy is tightened
Researchers ask for safer parking
The plan is revised after the event

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: The building returns to normal on stated conditions.
beats: Access is restored in steps
Counseling is offered
A summary goes to every lab

decisionPointExamples: lock down the whole building, or the wing
let police into restricted areas with an escort, or without
announce to the campus now, or after the facts
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a voicemail transcript, a badge log, a camera clip, a visitor sign-in, a police report
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: camera coverage has gaps, visitor logs are on paper, staff disagree on what they saw
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: campus security, police, the RO, the BSO and communications
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a lockdown, access or notification decision

addedThreatFamilies.label: Monitoring or access system degradation
addedThreatFamilies.description: The alarm, monitoring or access control system that watches the laboratories is down or wrong; the team works without it and decides what compensating checks to run.

phaseArc.title: Discovery
phaseArc.goal: The monitoring or access system stops reporting or reports nonsense.
beats: The freezer monitoring dashboard shows all units offline
Badge readers on a corridor stop working
Pressure alarms report values that do not change

phaseArc.title: Immediate actions and containment
phaseArc.goal: Staff start compensating checks by hand.
beats: Rounds on paper replace the dashboard
The RO asks for hourly checks of registered rooms
Facilities cannot say when the system will be back

phaseArc.title: Classify and notify
phaseArc.goal: Leaders decide which gaps must be reported and to whom.
beats: An outage in a registered area may need a note to the RO's records
Sponsors expect notice if samples are at risk
The institutional official asks for an impact summary

phaseArc.title: Investigate
phaseArc.goal: The vendor and facilities find the cause.
beats: The vendor blames a software update
A network change was made the day before
Logs for the gap are missing

phaseArc.title: Written reports
phaseArc.goal: Reports record the gap and the checks made.
beats: Paper rounds are incomplete
The report to the RO shows a different gap than the log
Counsel asks for the vendor contract

phaseArc.title: Corrective action
phaseArc.goal: The institution adds redundancy and tests it.
beats: A second path for alarms is proposed
Budget is short
The call-out test fails on the first try

phaseArc.title: Return to work
phaseArc.goal: Normal monitoring returns on stated conditions.
beats: Sensors are calibrated before use
Staff stop paper rounds in stages
A drill record is written

decisionPointExamples: staff rounds by hand through the night, or accept the risk
report the gap now, or when the system is back
move samples to units on another monitor
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a dashboard screenshot, a vendor ticket, a paper round sheet, a network change log, a call-out test result
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: the vendor is slow, rounds are incomplete, nobody holds the manual process
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: facilities, research IT, the lab managers, the vendor and the RO
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep the story at the level of what the organization decides and whom it tells: classification, stop-work, medical evaluation, notifications and their deadlines, continuity and messages. Name an agent only as a generic class or from the designer's reviewed list. Give no technique, protocol, growth, production, quantity, strain or modification detail for any agent.

decisionMustMention.description: a compensating check, a report or a move decision
